newsitem.title: CANADA: B.C. forest companies call off contract talks.
newsitem.headline: B.C. forest companies call off contract talks.

text.p: British Columbia forest companies on Monday called off contract talks with unionized workers until loggers in the Fraser Valley end a wildcat strike, a forest company spokesman said.

Keith Bennet, chief negotiator for Forest Industrial Relations, which represents about 65 forestry companies in British Columbia, said there was not much point for forest companies to sit down with the IWA-Canada union until the illegal job action was resolved.
"It is highly improper for us to sit down with them while this illegal action is going on," Bennett told Reuters.

Negotiations between the industry and 29,000 unionized workers in the lumber sector were slated to start on Monday but Bennett said the talks would be postponed until all striking workers returned to work.
"We're talking several months before negotiations are completed," he said.
An estimated 1,500 workers at International Forest Products Ltd were refusing to cross picket lines at eight or nine sawmills in the Fraser Valley, a prime logging area northeast of Vancouver.
The union has said it did not condone the strike, but understood it. A union official called the strike a "minor problem" but declined to comment on the forest industry's decision to delay the talks.
The union's current contract expires at midnight on June 14.
